gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's store prices that change its ranking. Anker now sells its first pick, the SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, for $1,199.99 (rival pages list $999.99). That is the same money as the FOSSiBOT F3600 Pro at $1,199 for 3,840 Wh, nearly twice the C2000's 2,048 Wh. It is also $300 more than the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at $899, which CNET measured within about 1.1 hours of the Anker on the same fridge. ChatGPT's 3 kWh 'margin' pick, the Jackery HomePower 3000 at $1,499, doesn't ship until Nov 28.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages theoutagebrief.com (2026-10-22 guide), homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/refrigerator and wattpowerstation.com (fridge guide). Yahoo/CNET returned 403. theoutagebrief prices the C2000 Gen 2 at $999.99 (Oct 15) and already has the DELTA 3 Max at $879 (Nov 9) and the Elite 200 V2 at $899. wattpowerstation has CNET hours with 'fridge hours per $100', but uses the old $999.99 C2000 price and no price dates. homepowerfacts lists the C2000 Gen 2 at $1,199.99 but as an undated 'list' price, next to estimated rather than measured hours. None of the three cited pages lists the FOSSiBOT F3600 Pro or its $1,199 price. None says that the HomePower 3000, HomePower 3600 Plus and Explorer 2000 v2 are pre-order or ship-later today. The DELTA 3 Max and Elite 200 V2 prices are already on rival pages, so I scored this 2, not 3.
decides: This confirms the Elite 200 V2 ($899, 26.32 h measured by CNET via wattpowerstation) as the value pick for a full 24 hours: $34 per measured fridge-hour against $44 for the C2000 Gen 2 at today's $1,199.99. For anyone who wants margin, ChatGPT's 3 kWh suggestion (HomePower 3000, $1,499, ships Nov 28) loses to the FOSSiBOT F3600 Pro: $1,199, 3,840 Wh, in stock. The FridgePower ($949, 23.43 h) and Dabbsson 2000L (21.00 h) fall short of 24 h on CNET's fridge, which rules them out.
